caption: A lakehouse in one picture: immutable raw files land in object storage, pipelines turn them into Parquet in progressively cleaner layers, a table format's metadata makes the silver and gold layers transactional, a catalog holds the pointer to each table's current snapshot, and every engine reads the same files through that catalog.
alt: Sources on the left send data into a raw zone of immutable compressed files in object storage. A pipeline parses them into a bronze zone of typed Parquet, then into silver and gold zones managed by an open table format whose metadata layer records snapshots, schema and partitions. A catalog maps table names to the current metadata. On the right, Spark, Trino, DuckDB and a cloud warehouse all query the same tables through the catalog.

groups.label: Object storage: one copy of the data
